clue.text: Try abandoning forced entry etc storming stronghold in determined attempt

indicators.note: storming suggests violent disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoning means the word try is left out of the words that follow it

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: A military assault: troops give up trying to force their way in and simply storm the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like the definition's verb, but it is the letters removed from 'entry'. 'storming' then rearranges FORCEDENETC into CONCERTEDEFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym phrase: a resolute, combined push at something is a determined attempt.

clue.text: See 10
Nosey girl comes up with a name for old Bob?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
with ... for marks a swap: the first pair of letters takes the place of the shilling letter
for here means in place of, completing the substitution signal

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A prying girl turns up with a nickname for an old fellow called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: In LASS one S (shilling, 'old Bob') is replaced by A N, giving LASAN, which reads upwards as the answer. A bob is the pre-decimal British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both relate to the nose: an adjective describing something of or through the nose.

clue.text: Waste from river flowing up over most of island

indicators.note: over means the reversed river covers the other piece, enclosing it
in a down clue, flowing up means the river's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Axe is a river in south-west England

indicators.note: most of means the island's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Crete is the Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Pollution: sewage from a river running uphill over most of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing up' turns the river to EXA, and 'over' has it enclose the island's shortened name. The Axe is a small river in Devon and Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: bodily discharges such as faeces and urine are waste matter.

clue.text: Road taxes left in place for coins when heading North

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters are read upwards
in means the letter for left goes inside the slot

parts.note: a slot in a machine is a place for coins

explanation.surface: Motorists' charges, with a coin slot left in place on the northbound road.
explanation.walkthrough: L inside SLOT gives SLLOT, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: charges paid to use a road, bridge or tunnel are road taxes.

clue.text: News department finished early as a couple gave up hope

indicators.note: finishing early means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the desk is a department of a newspaper, such as the news desk
paired means joined together as a couple

explanation.surface: Staff in a newsroom go home early, and a couple lose hope.
explanation.walkthrough: DESK cut short is DES, then PAIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to lose all hope of something is to have given up hope.

clue.text: Copper layer is cut to pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bed is a layer, as of rock or gravel

explanation.surface: A layer of copper is being cut into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookery term: food diced into small square chunks has been cut to pieces.

clue.text: See 9
Old asylum inmate after striking head timetabled to go mad

indicators.note: going mad suggests a wild rearrangement of the remaining letters
striking the head means the first letter of timetabled is removed

explanation.surface: An old lunatic, after hitting his head, has timetabled descending into madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timetabled' minus its first letter is IMETABLED, rearranged. Bedlam was the London hospital for the insane (Bethlem).
explanation.definitionFit: A historical word for a lunatic, after Bedlam, the London madhouse, so an old asylum inmate.

clue.text: Pairs of pictures showing yachts at sea without a following depression

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the depression

parts.note: a dip is a hollow or depression in the ground

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged
without means the letter a is taken out of yachts

explanation.surface: Paintings of yachts at sea, followed by a slump in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' leaves YCHTS, which 'at sea' rearranges to TYCHS.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific term: two hinged painted panels, often an altarpiece, form a pair of pictures.

clue.text: Game Of Thrones?

parts.note: the TV fantasy title, read literally as a game played with thrones, that is seats

explanation.surface: A nod to the hit fantasy TV series about the battle for the Iron Throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrones are just seats; the party game has players scrambling for seats when the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a party game where players compete for a dwindling number of seats.

clue.text: Dandy poet mixing with scum might make enjoyable entertainment

indicators.note: mixing tells us to blend the letters of the named words into a new order

explanation.surface: A foppish poet rubbing shoulders with lowlifes could make for fun entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a comic performing jokes solo to an audience is a form of enjoyable entertainment.

clue.text: Prehistoric structures, rough old pieces with a hint of Stonehenge

indicators.note: rough means roughly arranged, so the three letters are reordered

parts.note: men are the pieces in chess or draughts

indicators.note: a hint of means just the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Ancient monuments made of rough old stones, recalling Stonehenge.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: megalithic tombs of upright stones topped by a slab are prehistoric structures.

clue.text: Piece of land surrounding lake initially dug year in advance

indicators.note: surrounding means the plot of land goes round the lake's letter

parts.note: an area is a piece of land

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of dug is used

explanation.surface: A plot around a lake was dug a year ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonyms: something done before the time in question has been done beforehand, in advance.

clue.text: Excellent person to have because he made a blow-by-blow account?

indicators.note: to have means the excellent person holds the word for because

parts.note: a beaut is informal, chiefly Australian, for an excellent person or thing
for can mean because, as in 'for I was afraid'

explanation.surface: A splendid man to have around, as he gave a detailed account of every punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow-by-blow' looks like a fight commentary; the blows are winds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: Admiral Francis Beaufort devised the scale grading wind strength, literally an account of each blow.

clue.text: 'Art In A Bin' Shocked National Icon

indicators.note: shocked means jolted out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline: a binned artwork outrages a national treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem: the helmeted female figure with trident and shield personifies Britain, a national icon.

clue.text: Bog's not half ugly stench, a source of odorous seeds

parts.note: a fen is a bog or marsh; the 's is just the possessive of the surface

indicators.note: not half means only half of ugly is used, its first two letters

parts.note: a reek is a strong unpleasant smell, a stench

explanation.surface: A marsh with a pretty foul smell, coming from strong-smelling seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: this Mediterranean herb yields aromatic seeds used in curries, a source of odorous seeds.

clue.text: See 26
Important prison associated with an island

parts.note: major means important
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A major jail linked with an island, like Alcatraz.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective of origin: relating to the Balearic island off Spain, so associated with an island.

clue.text: Fiesta with band and conga in a fuss about nothing!

definitions.text: Fiesta with band and conga in a fuss about nothing!

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the zero
in a fuss means agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party with a band and a conga line, all a commotion over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: FIESTA BAND AND CONGA is rearranged around O. The whole clue also defines: a festive dance makes a fuss over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: making an unnecessary commotion over something trivial is a fuss about nothing.

clue.text: See 17
Old invaders, mainly Scandinavian, capturing one of our islands

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened word holds the island inside
mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian, especially old Norwegian
the Isle of Man is one of the British Isles

explanation.surface: Ancient raiders, mostly Scandinavian, seize a British island.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical example: William's men conquered England in 1066, so they were old invaders.

clue.text: A way of working up in this sort of thing to this extent

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the other word

parts.note: such means this sort of thing, as in 'such behaviour'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A working method gets going in this kind of thing to this degree.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for modus operandi; 'up' turns it to OM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent phrases of degree: 'that far' or 'to such a degree' means to this extent.

clue.text: See 1
See 17
Bad offer providing returns at first — urgently ask some questions

indicators.note: at first means the turned word comes before the rest
returns means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: if means providing, as in 'if it rains'

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor offer produces returns, so you start asking questions fast.
explanation.walkthrough: IF reversed gives FI, followed by OFFER rearranged as REOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to discharge questions in rapid succession is to urgently ask some.

clue.text: Auditor's candid — this currency's not legal tender

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so the word is as heard

parts.note: frank means candid

explanation.surface: An accountant speaks plainly: this money is no longer valid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but here means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact: the old French coin was replaced by the euro in 2002 and ceased to be legal tender.

clue.text: Love for acting in 9 drama

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
per means for, as in so much per head
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in military ranks like A/Captain

explanation.surface: A love of performing in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' refers to the first word of the 9 Across solution, qualifying 'drama'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre: a stage work sung throughout with orchestral accompaniment is a sung drama.

clue.text: See 26
VIP's attaché and junior women worked together

indicators.note: worked suggests kneading, so these letters are mixed up together

explanation.surface: A dignitary's attaché and some junior female staff cooperated.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone whose name carries influence and fame is a very important person.

clue.text: Welsh Rugby team in a lower position

definitions.meaning: a South Wales rugby union club named after its town
a poetic shortening of beneath, meaning below

explanation.surface: A Welsh rugby side languishing low in the league.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a town and rugby club near Swansea, and a literary word for below.

clue.text: Karate takes time to get things moving?

indicators.note: takes means the martial art holds the time letter inside

parts.note: karate is an art of kicks, a kicks art

explanation.surface: Doing karate takes a while before it gets you going.
explanation.walkthrough: Karate read as KICKS ART takes in T. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb: starting a motorbike engine with a kick pedal, so figuratively to get things moving.
